question.text: After Nicholas abdicated, he and his family were executed, paving the way for this Bolshevik ("BOWL-she-vick") leader to assume power.
question.clue: This politician attacked social democrats in his April Theses, and returned to Russia in a "sealed train" to oppose the Mensheviks.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about leaders with titles in common.
swap.text: Give the title last held by Nicholas II of Russia before he was killed in 1918.
swap.clue: It's not in Germany, but one holder of this title issued the Anti-Semitic May Laws, which prohibited the creation of new towns by Jews.

question.leadin: In the late 17th century, this ruler went on a Grand Embassy of Europe, exploring methods to Westernize his country.
question.text: Name this "Great" member of the Romanov dynasty.
question.clue: This monarch's half-sister Sophia was forced to become a nun after the streltsy, whom this monarch disbanded, revolted on her behalf.

swap.leadin: In this event, Father Gapon organized a peaceful march in St. Petersburg that was met by the Tsar's troops; hundreds of people were killed.
swap.text: Name this event, which started the 1905 Russian Revolution. The name of this event applies to numerous other massacres, including one of Irish protesters by the British army in 1972.
swap.clue: The first day of the Battle of Paardeberg during the Second Boer War was given this name, as was the beating of protesters by police during the Selma to Montgomery March.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the Eastern Front during World War II.
question.text: This Soviet general directed the counteroffensive at Stalingrad and the defense of Moscow before leading offensives into Germany and commanding occupation forces.
question.clue: This general assisted a future premier in arresting his rival Lavrentiy Beria.

swap.leadin: Upon learning of Islam's prohibitions on alcohol, a ruler of this polity exclaimed "drinking is the joy" of his people, and converted to Christianity instead.
swap.text: Name this polity, whose history is reported in Nestor's Primary Chronicle. One ruler of this polity, Vladimir the Great, ordered the mass baptism of its citizens in the Dnieper ("Knee-per") River during its Christianization.
swap.clue: Its leaders used a system of succession in which the throne would pass to the eldest brother of the deceased, called the rota or "ladder" system.

question.leadin: Name some things about famous battles won by Napoleon Bonaparte against those stone-cold warriors, the Russians.
question.text: At this battle, which occurred after Barclay de Tolly was relieved of command, Pyotr Bagration ("bug-rat-ee-OHN") was killed, and the French incurred enough casualties to force their eventual retreat.
question.clue: Pierre Bezhukov spends most of this battle in a battery at the Raevsky Redoubt, and Mikhael Kutusov is described as being inactive during it.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the political career of a certain revolutionary leader.
swap.text: Born with the last name Ulyanov, this expatriate was living in Switzerland when the Germans sent him to Russia in a sealed railroad car on March 1, 1917 to instigate a revolution and negotiate peace.
swap.clue: Edmund Wilson titled an intellectual history for this man's arrival at the Finland Station, which occurred after Germany financed a train trip from Switzerland for him and other "majority party" members.

question.text: This capital of the USSR was the site of the 1980 Olympics, as well as frequent "physical culture" parades in Red Square.
question.clue: This city traces its history to a post founded by Yuri of the Long Arm.

swap.leadin: In addition to the ball drop in Times Square, the New Year often sees regime change. For the stated points-.
swap.text: For 10 points, on December 31, 1999, this first president of the Russian Federation resigned.
swap.clue: After the Battle of Grozny, his government signed a ceasefire agreement in the First Chechen War.

question.text: This prior tsar spread rumors that the false Dmitry was a commoner. This tsar was the first non-Rurikid tsar, and his death precipitated the Time of Troubles.
question.clue: This play's fifth scene features Pimen writing a history of Rus and waking up the young monk Grigory Otrepev, who in the sixth scene has run off, leaving the message "I will be czar in Moscow".

swap.text: Under Andropov, the KGB put this physicist under house arrest, preventing him from claiming the 1975 Nobel Peace Prize for his work against nuclear proliferation. Earlier, he had been crucial in developing the Soviet hydrogen bomb.
swap.clue: This man's political activism led to him being exiled to Gorky.

question.leadin: It supposedly resulted in the poisoning of Andrey Zhdanov and Alexander Shcherbakov, and it was partly blamed on the international Jewry.
question.text: Name this supposed conspiracy of members of the titular profession to assassinate Soviet leaders, first reported in the January 13, 1953 issue of Pravda.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the dissolution of the Soviet Union.
swap.text: In order to revive stagnant economies, Mikhail Gorbachev introduced two reform oriented policies, one of which was perestroika. The other was this policy of openness that made government behavior more transparent.
swap.clue: Russian political policy that followed Gorbachev's 1985 rise to power. The result of this policy was a dramatic increase in political freedom, the release of a number of political prisoners, and loosened the state control of the media. The term means "openness" in Russian.

question.leadin: This philosopher declared that "The revolutionist is a doomed man" in a tract he wrote with Sergey Nechayev, Catechism of a Revolutionist.
question.text: Name this philosopher who outlined his beliefs in works such as Statism and Anarchy. Due to his feuds with Karl Marx, this philosopher was expelled from the International Workingmen's Association in 1872.
question.clue: His quarrel with Marx at the First International split the European communist movement. He argued for the education of the common man in an effort to enable society to rise up and destroy most institutions. For 15 points-name this author of God and the State, the chief propagator of nineteenth-century anarchism.

swap.leadin: This ruler's death prompted Frederick II of Prussia to claim that "The Messalina of the North is dead. Morta la Bestia."
swap.text: Name this empress of Russia and daughter of Peter the Great. The accession of her nephew Peter III to the throne following her death became known in Prussia as the Miracle of the House of Brandenburg.

question.text: This Russian tsar demanded that the Livonian confederation pay high taxes and occupied Dorpat and Narva, setting off the Livonian war.
question.answer: Ivan IV or Ivan the Terrible
question.clue: This son of Basil III prosecuted the Livonian War and suppressed Novgorod. Ruling from 1547 to 1584, this Rurikid was notable for maintaining the oprichina, a secret police force, and being an all-around mean dude.

swap.text: The leader of the pro-German government, Pavlo Skoropadskyi, revived the use of this title while leading Ukraine in 1918. This title was traditionally used by leaders of a sich until abolished by Catherine the Great.
swap.clue: Holders of this title, who carried a gem-encrusted mace called a bulawa ("boo-WAH-va"), were elected by the Sich ("seetch") Rada.

question.leadin: Here's a bonus on Russian names that, thankfully, did not get turned into a cheesy common links tossup. FTPE.
question.text: Three Rurik rulers of Moscow held this name. The first faced an invasion by Tamurlane that stopped short of Moscow, the second was known as "The Blind," and the third was the father of Ivan the Terrible.
question.clue: This grand prince of Moscow, who annexed Nizhny Novgorod and Murom and ruled from 1389 until 1425. His death led to a dynastic struggle between his eventual successor, that successor's uncle Yury, and Dmitri Shemyaka.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the medieval state of Kievan Rus.
swap.text: Much information about Vladimir and Yaroslav may be found in this foundational document of medieval Russian history, which compiles Russian, other Slavic, and Byzantine sources on eastern European events up to 1113.
swap.answerHtml: Russian Primary Chronicle [or Chronicle of Nestor; or Povest vremennykh let; or Tale of Bygone Years; prompt on Kiev Chronicle]
swap.clue: This work found in the Laurentian and Hypatian codices. It describes such events as the arrival of the Varangian brothers and the murder of Dir.
